title: Learning deterministic BPE merges
description: Quick definitions for fitting byte-pair rules, counting candidates, and retaining exact token bytes.

terms.definition: In this course, fitting starts with all 256 byte entries and learns ordered rules for merging neighboring tokens. Each new entry represents joined bytes; pieces need not be whole characters or words.
An ordered pair of neighboring token IDs in the current sequence for one training document, eligible for selection as the next merge rule.
The number of adjacent windows carrying a particular token pair in the current training documents. Overlapping windows count separately; windows never cross documents.

One fitting cycle while candidates remain: count current adjacent pairs, select a winner, add an entry for its joined bytes, and replace left to right without overlap in each document. The next round recounts the changed sequences.
A learned rule's zero-based position in the ordered BPE table. Rank records learning order, not frequency or token identity; the first rule has rank zero and receives token ID 256 here.
This course's rule for equal candidate counts: choose the smaller left numeric token ID, then the smaller right ID if the left IDs match.
A left-to-right pass that emits one merged token ID per match and consumes the two matched input tokens once. Unmatched tokens are copied; emitted tokens are not rescanned in that pass.
The exact ordered bytes represented by a token ID. Initial entries store one byte; learned entries join the two merged entries' bytes. A piece may be incomplete UTF-8.
The end of a training document, where adjacent-pair counting and replacement stop. Tokens in separate documents cannot form a pair; spaces inside one document remain ordinary bytes.
